Adam

We had a camera trap dataset long before I knew of camtrapR.  So after using camtrapR, we generated lots of scripts to identify all these kinds of hassles.  Stations without matching image-species-recordTable records, and vice versa, species records without a station. Images outside of the deployment dates in the station file, … Inconsistent names of stations and species, ...

Depending on the camtrapR function used, so you will get warnings, errors and mis-information.  If you are only using the info in the recordTable, for example, activity diel outputs will be okay. However as soon as you try mapping geographic distributions which requires species records with location, which is of course only in the station file, then the records with no station will not map.

I have 900 000 records in my recordTable and ~ 500 + stations so I understand the difficulty sorting missing and erroneous data.

All I can suggest is that you use camtrapR and pay close attention to the outputs.

I can share some of our experiences (in the form of Rmd files) and if they suggest help, I’ll provide the R scripts.  But much of the exercise depends on what questions you are asking.

David.

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Not all values of stationCol in recordTable are matched by rownames of camOp
parts: So it is ok to have stations in the camtraps data frame that do not exist in the recordtable (ie this station didn't catch anything)?

Yes, that is how it is supposed to be. The camera trap table contains information about all cameras (stations), no matter if they had any records or not. The record table contains only the actual records. So for a rare species you may well have hundreds of stations (rows in camera trap table), but only a one or handful of entries in the record table.
You only get an error if there is a station in the recordtable that doesn't exist in the camtraps right?

Yes.

In order to find mismatches between the entries of the station columns in the camera trap table and the record table, you could do something like:

# show all unique entries of the record table station column that are not in the camera trap station table
unique(recordTableSample$Station)[!unique(recordTableSample$Station) %in% camtraps$Station]

# show all unique entries of the camera trap station table station column that are not in record table
unique(camtraps$Station)[!unique(camtraps$Station) %in% unique(recordTableSample$Station)]
